Transferring/manipulating orbits, Intercepting/docking and landing are the three primary skills you need to learn to do manually.

Here is how I suggest learning it. This, of course isn't optimal, but it will get you there. Once you do it a few times, you can figure out how to optimize it.

First thing to check and see if you are on career mode, if you are, you will need to have Maneuver Nodes unlocked. This means you will need the Mission Control building upgraded at least once.

Second, if you have maneuver nodes unlocked, you need to create a new node in the right spot. The way I do this is, once in a stable Kerbin orbit with no inclination, get in the map mode and look at it top down and zoom out until I can see both the Mun and Kerbin. I then rotate it so the Mun is at the 12 O'Clock position.

Next, I create a node in my orbit at the 3 o'clock position, realtive to the Mun's 12 O'clock, that it 90 degrees to the right.

Once I have this maneuver node create, I expand the node to raise the Apoapsis. As the Apoapsis nears the Mun's orbit, you should see an encounter appear. This will turn the Maneuver Node's Yellow line Purple and a Mun Periapsis marker will appear.

If this doesn't happen do the following... Do not let the Apoapsis extend past the much Mun's orbit. Next Grab the maneuver node ring and slide it around your current orbit path until the encounter appears (notice that doing this vastly increases your delta-v requirements for that maneuver).

Burn appropriate for the node for the required amount of time to generate enough Delta-V until the orbit matched what you planned. Now, just coast until you hit the encounter (when you are just inside the purple encounter line)

Once you are in the encounter portion of the node, create a new node at the Mun Periapsis point and reduce it until you get a circular-ish orbit. When you get near the node, start burning appropriate for the node until it is where you set it up.

Voila, you are in a Munar Orbit.

I highly suggest that you get used to doing this manually. Once you know hot co find, execute and fix intercepts and just maneuver nodes in general, you should probably graduate to a plugin like Mechjeb and use it to create and execute maneuver nodes.

How to make a perfect maneuver node:

1) Place it anywhere on your orbit, don't worry about its location yet.

2) Adjust the prograde marker until your apoapsis is as high as Mun's orbit.

3) Click the maneuver node (the gray circle, not the colorful direction markers), and drag it around your orbit until you get a Mun encounter near your apoapsis.

4) Fine-tune with the prograde/retrograde markers until you have an apoapsis you like.

I start by creating a steady orbit around Kerbal. It's hard to walk you through everything so bare with me!

  1. When you have an orbit (circular or elliptical) press "M" (map key) and find your ship. A little ways ahead of it (maybe 5mins ahead?) on the orbit path, left click. Select "Add Maneuver".

  2. Play with the different vectors until you get an orbit either a) similar to the moons, or b) an elliptical, fly-by of the moon.

  3. Find the new marker on your navigation, and fire your engines at it as you approach the new navigation marker. This will assist you in adjusting your trajectory towards the moon.

  4. After that, it is a mess of adjusting your trajectory using the above method until you are in munar orbit!

and

dmesg | grep -i xf86-video-ati

To check for errors in loading your kernel module.

lsmod | grep -i -e xf86-video-ati -e radeon -e vga

One more thing that may help:

sudo lshw -c video

If you don't have lshw, do sudo apt-get install lshw.
